key_insight: LLM stakeholder agents can generate context-sensitive healthcare preferences, but deliberation and presentation-order bias can undermine their reliability as optimization weights.
engineering_relevance: Audit agent-generated preferences and propagate their uncertainty into optimization before using them in healthcare decision support.
method: Elicit explicit criterion ratings from stakeholder agents for outpatient appointment scheduling.
Infer implicit trade-offs from pairwise choices between emergency department configurations.
Evaluate preference reliability and compare robust weighted-sum optimization with average-weight decisions.
evidence_signal: Computational experiments found role-dependent explicit preferences, strong presentation-order effects in pairwise choices, and robust solutions that differed from average-weight solutions in most cases.
watch_item: Contextual information showed limited evidence of improving prediction on new comparison pairs beyond presentation order alone.
paper_title: On the possibilities and limitations of LLM-based multi-agent systems for multi-criteria decision-making in healthcare operations management
